standard.title: Choreograph dance for meaning
standard.description: choreograph dance by selecting and manipulating elements of dance and choreographic devices to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use elements of dance and simple choreographic devices in own dance works (AC9ADA6C01). They have not yet selected and manipulated devices with a clear rationale for how each choice communicates specific ideas, perspectives or meaning.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students choreograph dance where selections of elements and devices are deliberate and connected to intended ideas, perspectives and meaning.

nodes.label: Improvising to generate choreographic material
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use improvisation as a generative tool to produce movement material that can be selected and developed for choreographic purposes
nodes.minimum_width: Generate movement material through at least one improvisation with a specific focus (e.g. mood, theme, relationship); select at least two movement phrases worth developing
nodes.typical_width: Use improvisation with different focuses (mood, social relationships, thematic ideas) to generate a range of choreographic material; document and evaluate what each improvisation produces
wider: Improvise using movements and techniques from diverse styles — evaluate how importing movement vocabulary from other traditions generates unexpected choreographic possibilities
Use improvisation focused on communication of specific emotions or social relationships — document how the improvisation generates movement that carries expressive content
Experiment with using improvisation for a specific production context (music video, VR experience) — evaluate how the intended context shapes what movement is worth generating

response_modes.reason: Students need to build a repertoire of improvisation approaches — focused on different themes, emotions, contexts and movement sources — before they can select intelligently from improvised material. A single improvisation produces a narrow range of material; diverse improvisation approaches build the generative bank needed for purposeful choreographic selection.

success_criteria: Generates movement material through at least one focused improvisation
Selects at least two movement phrases with a reason for their potential
Improvisation has a clear focus — not just free movement

nodes.label: Selecting and developing movement with choreographic devices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select movement from improvisation and develop it using choreographic devices to communicate intended ideas or meaning
nodes.minimum_width: Select movement from improvisation and develop it using at least one choreographic device; explain how the device serves the intended meaning
nodes.typical_width: Select, combine, refine and sequence movement using choreographic devices such as transitions, variation and contrast, and forms such as binary, ternary or narrative; document how each device choice serves the choreographic intent
wider: Experiment with multiple structural forms (binary, ternary, narrative) and evaluate how each changes what the dance communicates — select the form that best serves the intended meaning
Develop movement sequences that portray characters or social relationships respectfully and empathetically — evaluate whether the choreographic choices achieve the intended portrayal
Create choreography for a specific production context (music video, immersive VR experience) — analyse how the context constrains and shapes choreographic decisions

response_modes.reason: Students commonly apply a single familiar choreographic device (e.g. repetition) without exploring whether other devices better serve the intended meaning. Working across multiple devices and structural forms — in different contexts with different communicative goals — builds the habit of purposeful device selection rather than defaulting to the familiar.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The production context direction — choreographing specifically for music video or VR — opens genuinely different choreographic problems. Students who engage here must reason about how spatial and temporal constraints of the medium shape what choreographic choices are available, which is a substantially richer challenge than choreographing for a live performance stage.
success_criteria: Uses at least one choreographic device to develop selected movement
Explains how the device serves the intended meaning or idea
Device choice is deliberate — not just applied by default

nodes.label: Documenting and evaluating choreographic choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can document their choreographic process and evaluate whether their choices successfully communicate the intended ideas, perspectives or meaning
nodes.minimum_width: Document at least two choreographic decisions made during the process; evaluate whether each decision contributed to the intended communication
nodes.typical_width: Document the choreographic process using journals, blogs, video or audio recordings; analyse and evaluate structural choices; explain what worked and what would change
wider: Analyse own choreographic process to identify the decisions that had most impact — evaluate what they reveal about own strengths and developing areas as a choreographer
Use video documentation of own choreography to evaluate structural choices against choreographic intent — identify specific moments where choices succeed or fall short
Compare two versions of the same choreographic material — one developed with extensive documentation and reflection, one without — and evaluate what the documentation process produced

response_modes.reason: Documenting and evaluating choreographic decisions is a reflective practice habit that develops through sustained cycles of making, documenting and evaluating. Students need repeated practice with the documentation cycle until it becomes integrated into the creative process rather than an afterthought.

This node brings together improvisation and material generation (Node 1), device selection and development (Node 2), and reflective practice from D02 into a documented evaluation of the whole choreographic process. Students who can make choreographic choices but cannot evaluate and document them have not met the standard's full demand.

success_criteria: Documents at least two choreographic decisions
Evaluates whether each decision contributed to the intended communication
Documentation uses dance terminology — not just 'it worked' or 'it didn't'
